reader.summary: The Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reached a critical threshold this week, with confirmed deaths surpassing 5,000 and total cases crossing 10,000, making it the deadliest Ebola epidemic in the country's history. The virus spread beyond the DRC, with linked cases confirmed in Kenya and Nigeria, prompting Uganda to impose a 21-day quarantine on citizens returning from Congo and the Central African Republic to tighten border controls. Violence against health workers intensified, with a nurse killed and another severely injured in an attack in eastern Congo while responding to a case. A three-shot vaccine trial also began. In the political and security sphere, the United States imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defense ministry over its support for M23 rebels in eastern Congo. Former president Joseph Kabila emerged as a new rebel leader, drawing sharp accusations from President Tshisekedi that he is acting as Rwanda's proxy. The controversial referendum law was passed without opposition support, and the C64 opposition platform met in Rome. On the economic front, DR Congo was removed from the FATF grey list, while a report linked gold smuggling to the Islamic State-linked ADF insurgency in the east.

Former president Joseph Kabila emerged as a new rebel leader, and President Tshisekedi accused him of being Rwanda's proxy in the east.
Uganda imposed a 21-day quarantine on its citizens returning from DR Congo and tightened border controls.
A controversial referendum law was adopted in DR Congo without opposition support, sparking political debate.
DR Congo was removed from the FATF grey list alongside Bulgaria, Ivory Coast, and Monaco.
A report found that gold smuggling through Uganda is financing the Islamic State-linked ADF insurgency in eastern Congo.
A three-shot Ebola vaccine trial began in DR Congo.

display.eli5:
DR Congo is dealing with a really bad Ebola outbreak right now. More than 5,000 people have died and over 10,000 have been sick. The virus has already jumped to Kenya and Nigeria. Next week, we expect it to reach yet another country, which will make neighbors even more nervous about their borders and travel rules.

At the same time, rebels called M23 are fighting the government in the east of the country. The United States just punished Rwanda for backing those rebels, and now the rebels are expected to push a new attack toward a town called Uvira. That would be the M23 offensive toward Uvira that we flagged as a key story.

The government also passed a new law about holding a referendum, but the opposition group C64 says it was done unfairly. Next week, they will take it to court. That is the referendum law challenge we are watching.

A surprise would be if someone in Europe or North America got sick with the same Ebola virus, which would make the whole world pay attention and could trigger a global travel scramble.

Round 2026-10-17:
This week in the DR Congo was defined by three converging crises. Former President Joseph Kabila formally joined the AFC/M23 rebel coalition in eastern Congo; Kinshasa denounced the move as a prelude to a 'generalized attack' and warned that Kabila's own political family was fracturing over it. The development raised fresh fears that ongoing peace efforts in the east could unravel. The Ebola outbreak also accelerated sharply. The virus spread to an eighth province bordering Central Africa, the UN warned the epidemic was growing 'exponentially,' and the Africa CDC revealed over $700 million in pledged response funds remained unaccounted for. Fearing contagion, mothers in affected areas skipped vital maternal and pediatric care, prompting authorities to launch an improved vaccination drive in Beni. Diplomatically, tensions flared with Brussels after Belgian police searched the homes of President Tshisekedi's relatives; the DRC presidency then restricted its staff's contact with the Belgian embassy.
